analysis: Integration of all 13 units: the PR changes only CI/advisory threat-review tooling (.github/scripts tests, threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_runner.py, budget_scan.py, diagnostics.py, the threat-model-review workflow) plus docs. It touches no provider, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest (TB-011, T-053..T-058), key custody (A-003), attestation (TB-009), fan helper (TB-010), or prefix cache (T-041) code, so no canonical provider threat is regressed. Cross-checked the replayed integration_source patches against the prior analyses. The tests assert fail-closed behavior: unplanned native calls raise BudgetStopped; the workload ceiling is 500 calls and 16384 output tokens; invalid policy, ceiling or token values raise ReviewUnavailable; there is no backup-provider fallback after a budget stop; incomplete or errored scans give clean()=False with an explicit human-review banner; plan_calls is invoked per stage and per integration round (test-threat-diagnostics.py asserts plans == [2,1]). The workflow change removes the maintainer workflow_dispatch/pr_number paid path (dispatch is unpaid preflight only), takes the base SHA only from the PR event, and raises the timeout to 60 minutes with a 3000s scanner deadline. This reduces paid-trigger attack surface. The raised call and token ceilings increase the worst-case Bedrock spend, but they are bounded and gated by the existing same-repo/fork opt-in. The diagnostics artifact adds only numeric/enum policy fields and no content. Residual uncertainty, which is a coverage limit rather than a finding: the full Bedrock.plan_calls, budget_runner and workflow YAML hunks were partly truncated or not replayed (integration_source complete=false, 63 omitted units). The docs claims and tests were therefore not checked against every production line. No security regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
